findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on missing or unreadable file
findings.failure_mode: untrusted path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError> and use .map_err(|e| LoadError::Io(e))

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value or out-of-range input
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV row aborts the entire load instead of returning a typed parse error
findings.fix: use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| ParseError::InvalidValue)? and validate range before cast

findings.problem: as u16 lossily truncates u32 values outside 0..=65535
findings.failure_mode: values 65536+ silently wrap to small u16, corrupting data without error
findings.fix: use u16::try_from(parsed).map_err(|_| ParseError::OutOfRange) and remove the as cast

findings.problem: parts[0] and parts[1] access Vec elements without bounds checking on split result
findings.failure_mode: empty line or single-field line panics with index-out-of-bounds
findings.fix: use split_once(',') and match on Ok((name, value_str)) or return ParseError::Invalid

findings.problem: println!("loaded {}", parts[0]) emits console I/O inside domain parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: pure calculation logic leaks side effects, breaking determinism and making the function untestable in isolation
findings.fix: move all logging to the shell layer; parse logic should be pure and return only data or errors

findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(fallible I/O) fused with parsing logic in a single function
findings.failure_mode: shell (I/O) and core (parsing) are inseparable, preventing pure-unit testing of parse logic and violating Functional Core / Imperative Shell
findings.fix: split into shell fn load_raw(path: &str) -> Result<String, IoError> and pure fn parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, ParseError>

findings.problem: load_frames returns Vec<Record> with no error type; all failures must panic
findings.failure_mode: any failure mode (missing file, bad line, bad value, out-of-range) collapses into a panic rather than a distinguishable typed error
findings.fix: define enum LoadError { Io(io::Error), Invalid, InvalidValue, OutOfRange }; return Result<Vec<Record>, LoadError>

findings.problem: raw String fields and primitive u16 cross the parse boundary without domain validation
findings.failure_mode: callers can construct Record with any name string and any u16 value, making illegal states representable
findings.fix: define Name(newtype wrapping validated non-empty String) and value: u16 validated in a smart constructor Record::new(name: Name, value_str: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseError>

findings.problem: no capacity cap or try_reserve on the per-line parts Vec or the output Vec<Record>
findings.failure_mode: unbounded allocation from hostile input can trigger OOM or excessive memory usage
findings.fix: add a domain max_rows cap; after parsing, call records.try_reserve(max_rows).map_err(|_| LoadError::Allocation)? before collecting

findings.problem: parse::<u32>() followed by as u16 has no checked range guard between the two operations
findings.failure_mode: overflow at cast boundary silently truncates; no checked conversion path exists
findings.fix: replace with u16::try_from(value).map_err(|_| ParseError::OutOfRange) for checked conversion

findings.problem: println! returns () but the call discards nothing explicitly; however, if replaced with fallible logging, the result would be ignored
findings.failure_mode: pattern encourages ignoring must-use I/O results
findings.fix: remove println entirely from core; if logging needed, use a fallible Logger that returns Result

findings.problem: Record uses raw String for name instead of a Name newtype
findings.failure_mode: any string including empty or whitespace-only values are representable as valid names
findings.fix: struct Name(String); impl Name { fn new(s: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseError> { ... } }
